column2: On the authority of Abū ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ʿAbdullāh ibn ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb (may Allah the Exalted be pleased with them both), who said: I heard the Messenger of Allah (Allah bless him and his family and grant them peace) say:

“Islam has been built upon five: testifying that there is no god but Allah and that Muḥammad is the Messenger of Allah, establishing the prayer, giving the zakāh, pilgrimage to the House, and fasting Ramaḍān.” Reported by al-Bukhārī and Muslim.
Buniya (“has been built”): has been founded.

“Testifying that there is no god but Allah”: in one narration, “Islam has been built upon five: upon Allah being worshipped and whatever is besides Him being disbelieved in,” which explains the meaning of the statement of tawḥīd.
“Establishing the prayer”: performing it constantly, with its conditions.
“Giving the zakāh”: giving it to those entitled to it.
“Pilgrimage to the House”: going to it to perform the rites counted among the pillars of Islam. “Fasting Ramaḍān”: refraining during its days from whatever breaks the fast, with an intention.
Knowing the pillars of the religion, which is also included in the hadith of Jibrīl above.
These five obligations are individual obligations (furūḍ al-aʿyān); they are not lifted from the rest when some people perform them.
It is permissible to say “Ramaḍān” without the word “month”.
